resolutions.researcher_notes: current_ref (archive.org/details/2023-09-27-122841) returns HTTP 200 but is a Community-Images screenshot (title '屏幕截图 2023 09 27 122841', tags 'China pipeline') with no OCR/legible text exposed via the page HTML or metadata — url_verifier fails on any Chinese token ('missing expected'), so it cannot be cited as verifying 'shelved' even though the link itself is live. Searched for a fresh source confirming shelved status specifically: the primary approval document for this project (桂发改能源〔2018〕1484号, read via Wayback at web.archive.org/web/20250517135052/http://fgw.gxzf.gov.cn/.../t10409787.shtml) is silent on current status (it is the 2018 approval, not a status update), and I found no news or government notice dated after 2018 reporting construction start, completion, or formal cancellation for this segment (灵川分输站/兴安分输站 turned up nothing). This matches the deep-sweep audit's own finding (rows/P4726.json) that no post-2018 evidence of construction exists, and that audit separately proposes a stale-dormancy Status change to 'cancelled' (Presumed) via the Update workflow — i.e. there IS a disagreement signal against the recorded 'shelved' value's continued accuracy, so per the ref-sweep rule I am not proposing a ref for it here; leaving UNRESOLVED for Update to handle the status question. WebSearch budget for this session was exhausted before I could run additional targeted searches for this specific unit.

current_ref (t10409858.shtml on fgw.gxzf.gov.cn) is geo-blocked (ConnectTimeout) with zero Wayback snapshots (checked archive.org's availability API) — a legitimate dead end, not pursued further. Fresh search found the sibling approval document for THIS exact project, 桂发改能源〔2018〕1484号 '广西壮族自治区发展和改革委员会关于广西天然气支线管网项目桂林-灵川-兴安天然气支线管道工程项目核准的批复' (t10409787.shtml, same fgw.gxzf.gov.cn approval series, live via Wayback 2025-05-17 snapshot). It approves construction of a '天然气支线管道' (natural gas branch pipeline) — confirms Fuel=Gas directly. Single source (gas.in-en.com's matching 2019-01-18 news writeup on this same project returns 403 to any UA tested and has no Wayback snapshot, so could not be used as a second independent citation) — tier medium.

Same dead-end/replacement reasoning as the Fuel unit above (current_ref t10409858.shtml geo-blocked, zero Wayback snapshots). The approval document (t10409787.shtml) explicitly approves a '天然气支线管道工程' (gas branch/trunk transmission pipeline project) linking distribution stations at Guilin/Lingchuan/Xing'an — consistent with GEM's PipelineType=transmission (a branch line off the provincial transmission grid, not a local distribution main). Single source, tier medium.

Recorded value is ProposalYear=2021, ProposalMonth=7, with no current_ref. All dated milestones I can find for this project's proposal/approval stage are from 2018, not 2021: the Guilin DRC's request to the provincial DRC (市发改报字〔2018〕366号), the builder's own request (广投管网报〔2018〕212号), and the provincial approval itself dated 2018-12-25 (桂发改能源〔2018〕1484号, read via Wayback). A companion trade-press writeup (gas.in-en.com, 2019-01-18) reporting the same approval could not be fetched (403/no snapshot) but its own headline/date is consistent with late-2018/early-2019, not 2021. I found nothing dated 2021 tied to this project's proposal stage. This is a disagreement with the recorded value, not a confirmation — per the ref-sweep rule I am not proposing a ref for a different value; leaving UNRESOLVED. (The deep-sweep audit for this row independently flagged the same 2021-vs-2018 mismatch as a likely data-entry error, recommending correction via Update — see rows/P4726.json.)

Approval document states verbatim '设计输量为2.2亿立方米/年' (design annual throughput 220 million m3/year) = 0.22 bcm/y — exact match to the recorded Capacity/CapacityUnits. Single source (the matching gas.in-en.com news writeup, whose own headline quotes this same capacity figure, is blocked/unarchived — see notes above), tier medium.

Recorded value is Diameter=273.10mm. This is a value disagreement, not a confirmation, so per the ref-sweep rule I am not proposing a ref for the recorded 273.10mm figure; leaving UNRESOLVED.
